title: appointments.appointments.reschedule
description: Moves an appointment to another slot. Since appointments#10 the caller says WHEN and, if it wants, for how long — nothing else: the end of the slot is computed by the handler (start + duration), the current duration and the professional come from the appointment's own row, and the move is refused when it lands on a blocked period or breaks the hub's minimum notice / maximum advance. `end_datetime` is gone: an end that did not match its own duration was a row nobody could explain. Since appointments#142 it also carries WHO is asking (`channel`, and `customer_id` on the customer channel): moving an appointment on behalf of a client is refused when that appointment belongs to somebody else.

duration_minutes.description: Optional. When omitted the appointment keeps the length it already had.

channel.description: Who is moving the appointment: `staff` (someone operating the hub, the default — the agenda screen sends no channel and keeps moving any appointment: it is its own agenda) or `customer` (the client through an external channel, bound to say who they are with `customer_id`).

customer_id.description: Who is asking, on the `customer` channel (appointments#142): the id of that client in `customers`, as the external channel resolved them (the WhatsApp automation looks the client up by phone before listing anything). The move is refused when the appointment belongs to somebody else. MANDATORY whenever `channel` is `customer`, and applied by the handler rather than here: it is a rule about two fields at once, decided against the appointment row this schema cannot see. The staff channel never sends it.

allow_past.description: appointments#156 — the COUNTER's declaration that the new start has already happened: the client who arrived late and was seen at 11:30 instead of 11:00, so the agenda tells the truth. It excuses the PAST alone (a start still to come keeps `min_booking_notice` unless `allow_short_notice` is declared too); opening hours, blocked time and overlap still judge the move. Ignored on the `customer` channel: the client cannot move her appointment into yesterday.

allow_short_notice.description: appointments#165 — the COUNTER's declaration that it moves the appointment inside `min_booking_notice`: the client of 13:00 who arrived early and can be seen in half an hour. The minimum notice is the window of the CUSTOMER's booking; the receptionist with the agenda in front of her is who it protects. It excuses the minimum notice ALONE: `max_advance_booking`, the opening hours, blocked time and overlap still apply. Ignored on the `customer` channel, which keeps the notice.
